construct: Most local anesthetics are weak bases. Acidic tissue shifts the drug toward the protonated ionized form, reducing the nonionized lipid-soluble fraction available to cross neuronal membranes and reach intracellular sodium-channel binding sites.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Local anesthetics are weak bases. Acidic infected tissue increases protonation, lowering the nonionized lipid-soluble fraction that can cross the axonal membrane; fewer molecules reach the intracellular sodium-channel site, reducing anesthetic efficacy.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: The protonated form can bind the sodium channel after gaining intracellular access, so saying 'ionized drug is inactive' would be imprecise. The keyed statement correctly focuses on reduced membrane diffusion caused by a smaller nonionized fraction in acidic tissue.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: Independent reread found no authoritative basis to reverse the key and no alternative option remains defensible at the requested answer granularity.

correction_history.final_construct: Reduced local-anesthetic efficacy in infected acidic tissue
